sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. iCodex is a publishing-workflow technology and services business diversifying into domestic IT/project execution, not yet a demonstrated recurring SaaS compounder. Revenue grew at 39.18% over FY21–FY26, but FY26 PAT fell 20.80%, operating cash conversion was 0.23×, and capitalized development plus project deposits tie up substantial funding. The apparently modest 8.87× current-share P/E at the secondary ₹40.25 reference is not enough to overcome unresolved capital-application and funding bridges. BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS. This is a research-only execution/funding special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder or an instruction to trade. The decisive next evidence is a reconciled asset/proceeds ledger, accessible cash and facilities, collected project milestones and attributable software/project returns.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact researched identity: iCodex Publishing Solutions Limited; ISIN INE111601014; BSE 544483; official master ticker ICODEX$ and series SM. A proposed iCodex Limited rename received shareholder approval, but an effective ROC/exchange rename was not verified by 20 October 2026. Cutoff is 20 October; the price is the secondary 19 October 2026 last trade of ₹40.25, not an executable quote. Current issued shares are 15,637,020, giving ₹62.9390 crore market capitalization. Financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP/AS, FY21–FY26; the latest verified TTM is FY26 and H1FY27 is ND. The horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a 15% nominal INR pretax equity hurdle, no dividends and illustrative ₹5 lakh position. Governance and historical reported levels have Medium confidence; incremental returns, current funding, market implementation and valuation confidence are Low. Overall investment confidence is Low. G1 is Conditional; G2/G3/G4 are Hold — unresolved. None is labeled an evidenced default, theft or suspension.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 factor audits and exact original-weight arithmetic are supplied below. GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 4, EARN 4, R NS, D 4, P NS and L NS. BQS known weighted contribution is 4.10 at 88% coverage, with mathematical missing-data bound 4.22–5.30. GQS known contribution is 5.20 at 85% coverage, bound 5.35–6.70. IAS known contribution is 0.80 at 20% coverage, bound 1.60–8.80 because its BQS input is also NS. There is no weight redistribution, imputed midpoint or rankable point. No governance/funding numeric override is applied: the gates are unresolved rather than evidenced failures and CAP is unknown, not assigned ≤3. Moving uncertain GOV and CASH by one point moves BQS known sum by ±0.30 combined, GQS by ±0.10 and does not repair missing factors. GQS means Growth Quality, not governance. The aggregates are never added together.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company builds manuscript, editorial and publishing workflow products and sells software development, BPM/editorial operations, and application/IT support. FY25 revenue mix was ₹3.78 crore software (17.28%), ₹5.342 crore BPM (24.42%) and ₹12.7554 crore support/IT (58.30%). FY24 software was ₹4.6605 crore and IT/support only ₹0.5862 crore, so the headline growth is not evidence of expanding subscription licenses. FY26 export revenue declined 28.44% to ₹6.5473 crore, while domestic revenue rose 52.29% to ₹19.384 crore. Labor and service execution remain material: employee expense nearly doubled to ₹11.4199 crore, with 127 employees. Capitalized software, deployment work and labor-intensive operational support must be analyzed separately. The 2025 VEC contract is a back-to-back execution arrangement, not a verified direct PSU recurring-revenue franchise. Retained company revenue is forecast around ₹60 crore versus roughly ₹75 crore underlying projects, with forecast profit around ₹3 crore and ₹10 crore performance funding required. No ARR, retention, churn, renewal uplift or product-specific margin is disclosed.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Domain know-how and integration into publishing workflows can reduce customer inconvenience and provide useful niche positioning. They do not automatically create a moat: contracts are nonexclusive and short-notice terminable, and FY25 top-five concentration remained 99.28%. The top customer improved to 41.70% from 100% in each of FY23 and FY24, genuine progress but not broad diversification. Datamatics/Lumina, including acquired TNQTech, markets AI content workflows; it is treated as one group comparison rather than three independent peers. Integra's June 2026 EditorialPilot/ScholarOne integration shows that automated editorial assistance is contestable. MPS is specifically identified as a competitor in the issuer prospectus, but current comparable market metrics were not verified, so none are fabricated. These are operational comparators, not mechanically interchangeable valuation peers. MOAT 4 reflects limited demonstrated differentiation; a stronger assessment needs renewal cohorts, pricing persistence, customer migration costs and independently measured productivity gains retained by iCodex rather than passed through to clients.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue is ₹4.96460, 8.17762, 9.5367, 10.4007, 21.8775 and 25.9313 crore for FY21–FY26. These six observations give 39.18% five-year CAGR; FY23–FY26 gives 39.58% three-year CAGR. The five-year window was chosen before scoring; the numerical starting score is 9, reduced only to the Medium-confidence ceiling of 8. No additional small-base or single-half-year trajectory penalty is applied. Annual rupee additions and YoY growth are reproduced in the historical model. FY26 adds ₹4.0538 crore versus ₹11.4768 crore FY25. H1FY26 grew 28.14% in revenue and H2 9.09%; H2 PAT fell sharply, indicating growth and profit quality have diverged. Software revenue fell during FY25 while support/IT drove expansion. No acquired contribution is identified in reviewed records, but exact organic price/volume and customer win decomposition is ND. The ₹75 crore headline VEC underlying project value is not booked revenue, not the company's ₹60 crore estimated scope, and not a recurring annual growth commitment.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Runway comes from automating scholarly workflows and executing identifiable domestic projects, not a generic AI market-size claim. VEC offers specific access, but its ₹3 crore estimated profit on ₹60 crore revenue implies only 5% project profit, with no precise timeline or PAT definition and with ₹10 crore performance deposit before ordinary working capital. Comparing that lifetime profit with the deposit alone would ignore duration, collection risk and other capital, so it is not a 30% annual ROIC. FY26 intangible development remains ₹14.0137 crore and digital CWIP ₹7.4595 crore, with substantial spending ahead of attributed earnings. A current operating-capital bridge is provided, and 3/5-year observed financing proxies are shown, but these do not identify return on new tools or project cohorts. CAP remains NS. GQS therefore remains NS despite strong historical revenue growth. The model explicitly cash-funds development and charges recurring development against terminal EBITDA. Software completion, customers paying for it, and returns above a reasoned 14–18% nominal INR analytical capital-cost range must be demonstrated separately.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Governance concerns are specific and dated. IPO funds temporarily supported CC in April 2026, were restored by 30 April and swept in June; management acknowledges improper process, denies permanent diversion and reports remediation. The August shareholder vote actually passed, approving the ₹9.07 crore working-capital redirection and ₹1.34 crore interiors ratification. These later approvals resolve permission questions, not whether the remaining commitments were canceled or how spending maps to assets. Related-party prior approvals were missed and later ratified on 11 March; disclosed director plus family remuneration/fees totals ₹1.2757 crore, about 17.98% of FY26 PAT, but pricing abuse is not proven. Secretarial observations also cover disclosure and insider-trading-control processes, with management responses retained. Positive counterevidence includes unmodified statutory reporting, no reported fraud/default, revenue growth and completed software transfers. Execution remains mixed: prospectus staffing ambition near 200 contrasts with 127 at FY26, development and object deployment timelines shifted, and H2 profitability weakened. No automatic fraud label or governance override is justified on the reviewed evidence.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Operating EBITDA is PBT minus other income plus finance cost plus D&A, giving ₹10.7029 crore FY26; EBIT is ₹9.9533 crore. Reported PAT is ₹7.0938 crore and a transparent other-income-excluded sensitivity is ₹6.62333 crore, not an assertion of tax-normalized statutory profit. CFO bridges ₹10.9675 crore pre-working-capital operating cash less ₹5.2896 crore working-capital absorption and ₹4.0353 crore cash tax to ₹1.6426 crore. CFO minus cash capex is −₹13.1461 crore; financing-classified interest makes owner cash lower still. Forecast ONWC excludes ₹0.0355 crore accrued bank interest, paid once as legacy financing cash flow in FY27. Four-year cumulative CFO/PAT is 0.58746 and cumulative reported FCF −₹16.4405 crore. Average receivable days use total revenue as a disclosed credit-sales proxy, while closing FY26 days are about 162.7. Interest coverage looks strong on reported EBIT, but restricted cash and heavy capitalized spending make it incomplete.

Broad March cash ₹12.7837 crore is not all liquidity: only ₹0.114 crore is clearly free, ₹0.0573 escrow and ₹12.6124 FDs are restricted/lien-marked. June's ₹9.07 crore IPO remainder overlaps deposits and is not added again. Book debt ₹7.0483 crore includes the CC balance and director loan; uncleared cheques are already reflected and are not deducted a second time. The ₹10.556 crore security-deposit balance is largely explained by the ₹10 crore VEC requirement, while exact allocation and refund timing remain unverified. Office/interior application, capital advances, digital CWIP and ₹9.0743 crore remaining commitments require a ledger bridge. Tax dispute ₹3.0724 crore is a contested contingent claim, not an admitted debt. DTL ₹0.4221 and employee provisions ₹0.3551 are reserved once in terminal equity.

The IPO fresh-share count rose 27.74%, diluting prior holders by 21.72%; these are different percentages. The bonus itself did not economically dilute holders. OFS proceeds never enter company cash. Net financial-statement fresh proceeds ₹30.1666 crore and the monitoring expense framework differ by ₹0.7574 crore on costs, requiring scope/timing explanation. FY25 restatement/annual rounding and bank-deposit cash-flow presentation differences are retained rather than silently mixed; FY21/22 reported EPS denominators and FY26 4.93 versus 5.01 EPS require separate caution.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹40.25, current-share market capitalization is ₹62.9390 crore, reported P/E 8.87×, P/B 1.12× and EV/reported EBITDA 6.53× when only ₹0.114 crore free cash is netted against dated debt. Price divided by historical weighted EPS would give 8.16×, a different denominator; current issued claims are the equity valuation basis. Reported FCF yield is negative 20.89%. These are dated cross-checks, not fair values.

The principal model forecasts FY27–FY32 revenue, margins, taxes, interest, working capital, development, maintenance and outstanding capital commitments; only cash through 19 October 2031 is retained. FY32's 202/366-year cash fraction respects the leap year. Terminal value uses operating EBITDA less recurring development cash spending at 6×/9×/12× bear/base/bull multiples. Required cash reserves, signed cash deficits, debt and other claims remain in the equity bridge. No separate value is added for operational property, the VEC deposit or already-counted FDs. A current-share P/E reverse calculation is a second method, not independent proof of funding.

Base/bear/bull maximum diagnostic funding gaps are ₹5.63/17.74/4.71 crore, including pre-entry shortfalls, even after an explicitly hypothetical August release of ₹9.07 crore IPO funds. These are assumption-driven gaps, not observed defaults. All ordinary returns, ordinary entry prices and breached non-rescue returns are null. Separate counterfactual rescues raise equity at ₹20 with 3% fees and explicit dilution; base rescue needs gross ₹5.8078 crore, expands shares 18.57% and dilutes old holders 15.66%. Its conditional terminal value is ₹31.64 per diluted share and five-year return about −5.08% after illustrative 1% each-way costs, while bull and bear differ widely. These are not normal targets because the historical rescue did not occur and debt rollover/access remains unverified. Sensitivities include growth/multiple, collection days/margins, development, commitments, tax, deposit replacement, FD availability, credit and no rollover; 12/15/18% hurdle prices exist only within separately labeled rescues.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The permanent-loss path is correlated rather than a single lower exit multiple: concentrated clients delay collections, labor and project costs remain, capitalized tools fail to monetize, the performance deposit stays tied or must be replaced, and restricted FDs cannot finance obligations. Equity then bears adverse recapitalization, write-offs or low recovery even if reported EBITDA remains positive. The linked stress makes explicit these cash claims; ordinary share-price downside cannot be responsibly stated as a verified target with current financing unknown. The counterfactual fully funded bear still has negative signed residual equity, so common-equity payoff is zero in that illustrative case. Impairment risk is High, not a claim of present insolvency. The strongest bullish counterargument is real revenue growth, substantial book equity, signed project access, new approved facilities and permitted use of IPO funds; if collected cash and effective drawability reconcile, funding risk could fall sharply. The thesis-break variable is inability to convert contract/development spending into cash while meeting obligations without repeated adverse dilution.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A fivefold outcome requires 37.97% annualized shareholder wealth growth over five years, and tenfold requires 58.49%. At unchanged current shares, a 12× terminal P/E and 10% net margin, fivefold would require approximately ₹262.25 crore revenue and ₹26.22 crore PAT; tenfold ₹524.49 crore revenue and ₹52.45 crore PAT. These imply revenue CAGRs of 58.85% and 82.47% respectively from FY26, before any dilution. Such assumptions are more demanding than the 39.18% historical revenue CAGR and far above the current base-case scale. Higher margins or multiples reduce the arithmetic requirement but do not prove them; the VEC estimated 5% project profit margin argues against carrying historical software margins indiscriminately into larger project revenues. There is no supported probability or compounder designation. Strong cash collections, attributable return on development, repeatable customer wins and financeable scale would be prerequisites, not optional upside.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor collected revenue rather than project headlines. Request the current cash/lien/facility reconciliation and office/asset ledger immediately because these decide G2/G3. At the next available half-year, compare CFO, receivables ageing and average/closing collection days with FY26: CFO/PAT 0.232, receivables ₹11.5597 crore and closing collection days 162.7. Improvement needs collections, not mere reclassification or unpaid suppliers. Track actual VEC retained revenue, project profit and deposit release against ₹60/3/10 crore disclosed estimates/requirement. By March 2027 compare ₹14.0137 crore development completion with paid customers and product-level returns; completion alone is insufficient. Check whether the ₹9.0743 crore commitment was paid, formally canceled or remains binding. Review the next monitoring report for authorized fund use and the restoration controls promised after April. Check tax appeal decisions and the ₹3.0724 crore exposure separately. Verify effective legal-name change, fresh dilution, new pledges and current lot/restriction notices. Before any implementation conclusion obtain complete BSE traded-value/no-print and bid/ask data; do not rely on the 48 observed secondary days.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification is Hold — unresolved, research priority only. BQS/GQS/IAS are NS and are not eligible for numerical quality, growth-quality or investment rankings. This is not a watchlist merely waiting for a lower price: price cannot repair missing incremental economics, unresolved asset application or unverified funding. No evidence-backed compounder designation, favorable investment eligibility or automatic sell instruction follows. The ordinary entry range remains null until G2/G3 and implementation evidence improve. For an existing shareholder, the issue is financial clarity, funding and execution rather than purchase-price anchoring; holdings, taxes and executable depth are not supplied. Revisit after reconciliation of assets/proceeds, current bank access, collected milestones and a demonstrated return on additional development capital. The conditional rescue prices are stress diagnostics only, never a price-based shortcut around those requirements.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source register identifies original issuer filings, dates, page locators and SHA-256 hashes. Original PDFs, extracted text, screenshots and shareholder-level records remain outside analytical backups. Backups contain safe financial inputs, analysis and executable calculations; a source-free reproduction verifies calculations, not re-authentication of original documents. Material gaps are explicit: no H1FY27 result by cutoff; no ARR/retention/product margin or attributable cohort return; incomplete current FD/facility/commitment reconciliation; unclear office-to-asset mapping and issue-cost allocation; historical EPS denominator discrepancies; incomplete official liquidity and order-book evidence. Small FY25 restatement differences and cash-flow deposit reclassifications are not mislabeled as fraud. All financial amounts are ₹crore unless shares, per-share prices or percentages are explicitly labeled. No external source published after cutoff is used for a financial outcome; sources were retrieved on 21 October 2026 to reconstruct the 20 October information set. Source confidence and forecast uncertainty are distinguished. This is analytical research, not personalized financial advice or trade execution.

evidence.locator: Debt note and 22 April board outcome.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: CARO records no default/wilful default and no identified material going-concern uncertainty as of audit date. No signed current drawability/overlap schedule was located.
evidence.analytical_effect: G3 Hold, not evidenced default. Model total-limit and incremental-credit possibilities separately.

evidence.claim: Monitoring records temporary 5.25 crore transfers from IPO monitoring funds to CC in April, restored on 30 April and swept to FDs on 20 June. Without the transfers CC drawings would have exceeded the limit.
evidence.locator: Monitor printed pp 3, 7-9.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Management acknowledges an improper temporary mechanism, reports no permanent diversion and strengthened controls. Restoration is recognized; theft or fraud is not asserted.
evidence.analytical_effect: GOV 4, G1 Conditional; evidence is stronger than a generic governance warning but not sufficient for severe-abuse override.

evidence.claim: Shareholders passed both 14 August 2026 special resolutions by 99.811%: redirect 9.07 crore unused office/hardware IPO objects to working capital, and ratify 1.34 crore interiors deviation.
evidence.locator: Notice explanatory statement and actual voting/scrutineer tables.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: The company cites business requirements and confirms an approved revised use through March 2027. Approval does not itself demonstrate cash availability or cancel existing contractual obligations.
evidence.analytical_effect: Distinguish resolved authorization from unresolved cash/application reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Audited capital commitments are 17.8143 crore gross less 8.74 crore incurred = 9.0743 crore outstanding. Monitoring reports 7.40 crore office plus 1.34 crore interiors used, while annual PPE is only 0.3538 crore and 7.4595 crore CWIP is described as digital development.
evidence.locator: Commitments note, monitoring objects table and annual digital-development policy.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Classification, advances, timing or allocation may explain some difference; no allegation of missing cash is made. Statutory opinion is unmodified.
evidence.analytical_effect: G2 Hold until invoice/asset-register/capital-advance/commitment mapping is supplied; conservative model retains remaining commitment.

evidence.claim: Capitalized FY26 development additions are 7.3009 crore; digital CWIP additions 7.4595; other PPE 0.0283. Together they reconcile exactly to 14.7887 cash capex. Transfers of 2.1418 crore into completed software are internal, not extra capex.
evidence.locator: Fixed/intangible/CWIP notes and cash flow.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Useful software assets can generate future profits; remaining 14.0137 crore development is expected to complete by March 2027. No cohort monetization or impairment downside assessment with realized returns is supplied.
evidence.analytical_effect: Terminal EBITDA is charged for recurring development spending; do not mistake capitalization-led margin for free cash.

evidence.claim: Tax claims total 3.0724 crore across four assessment years regarding 80-IAC deductions, including interest. Appeals are pending; penalty proceedings are held in abeyance; no provision is recognized based on favorable legal advice.
evidence.locator: Contingency and tax notes.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Management believes its case is strong. No adverse final adjudication located by cutoff.
evidence.analytical_effect: Separate adverse-tax cash stress, not base-case payable or proved default.

evidence.claim: FY26 director remuneration is 0.87 crore and disclosed family professional fees total 0.4057 crore. Secretarial review records related-party prior-approval lapses later ratified on 11 March 2026, alongside SDD/ODR and filing-control weaknesses.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 42-45 and related-party note.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Management reports corrective action and promises prior approvals. Transactions alone do not establish unfair pricing or abusive diversion.
evidence.analytical_effect: Assess recurrence, proportionality and minority controls rather than automatic fraud labeling.

evidence.claim: IPO fresh proceeds were 34.6392 crore; OFS 7.39296 crore belongs to selling holders, not the company. Financial statements charge 4.4726 crore against premium; monitoring uses 5.23 crore issue costs and 29.41 net proceeds.
evidence.locator: Share premium/cash flow; IPO terms; monitor.
evidence.status: Fresh share bridge verified; fee-scope reconciliation open
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: Different issue/OFS, allocation or timing perimeters may explain the 0.7574 crore expense difference. It is not automatically a cash loss.
evidence.analytical_effect: Do not add OFS, prepaid reimbursement or restricted cash twice. Retain fee bridge in G2 open questions.

evidence.claim: H1FY26 revenue/PAT 13.8949/5.4994 crore and H2 12.0364/1.5944 show H2 PAT down 65.57% YoY despite revenue up 9.09%. FY26 reported EPS is 4.93 in detailed audited accounts versus 5.01 in initial result filing.
evidence.locator: H1 statement and audited H2/annual filings.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: FY26 annual revenue still rose 18.53%; employee expansion and project mix can explain lower margins. H1FY27 was not located by cutoff, so no current-quarter rebound is assumed.
evidence.analytical_effect: EARN 4; use current share-count earnings for valuation rather than blending conflicting weighted EPS.

evidence.claim: Official lot is 1,200; at secondary 19 October close 40.25 one lot costs 48,300. Of 60 shared calendar sessions only 48 issuer observations were found; of 20, only 12.
evidence.locator: Historical table and official master.
evidence.status: Secondary trade records; incomplete executable-liquidity evidence
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: There are observed trading prints, including 1,200 shares on 19 October; missing dates are unknown, not zero. Public holding 35.56% is not effective float.
evidence.analytical_effect: L NS and G4 Hold. Observed-only 5% capacity proxy 72.2 days for 5 lakh, but no whole lot fits that assumed daily participation.

evidence.claim: Datamatics/Lumina describes AI-powered content workflows and TNQTech acquisition; Integra announced ScholarOne-integrated EditorialPilot in June 2026; issuer prospectus names MPS among competitors.
evidence.locator: Datamatics annual business discussion; Integra dated 25 June 2026 item; prospectus p 134.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: iCodex has niche publishing expertise and modular tools, but established vendors also offer workflow automation and AI. Scale itself does not prove peer superiority.
evidence.analytical_effect: No standalone AI moat, no duplicated Datamatics/Lumina/TNQ peers, no invented peer market multiples.

evidence.claim: FY26 financing-capital proxy 50.5719 crore plus accrued bank interest 0.0355, DTL 0.4221 and employee provisions 0.3551 less nonoperating tax/FD interest assets 0.3152 reconciles to 51.0694 crore operating capital including performance deposits and unfinished development.
evidence.locator: Balance sheet and detailed current/noncurrent asset notes.
evidence.counterevidence_or_company_response: There is a reconciled current accounting base, but no consistent multiyear project attribution, mature-cohort returns or software retention economics.
evidence.analytical_effect: Current ROIC and observed 3/5-year financing proxies are not substitutes for CAP; CAP NS.

formulas.reported_fcf_proxy: CFO - cash operating capex, before financing-classified interest
formulas.onwc_opening: Receivables 11.5597 + unbilled 0.5229 + prepayments 0.1160 + advances 0.0087 + operating current assets 0.1940 - payables 0.1053 - other operating liabilities 1.9153 (1.9508 less 0.0355 accrued interest); excludes cash, debt, FD interest and tax. Legacy accrued interest 0.0355 is paid once in FY27 financing cash flow.
formulas.forecast_onwc: Revenue * (receivable_days/365 - 0.04); -4% is explicit net other operating current liability assumption.
formulas.terminal_ev: max(0, EBITDA - recurring development cash charge) * stated multiple; maintenance capex shown in cash model, no property added.
formulas.terminal_common_equity: Operating EV + signed modeled cash - required operating cash reserve - debt - deferred tax and employee provisions; no separate deposit/property/FD addbacks.
formulas.tax: Forecast max(0, EBIT-interest)*30%; contested historical tax separate stress.
formulas.cashflow_interpolation: Linear within fiscal year, event at 15 August for hypothetical IPO use; interim claims and capex timing therefore uncertain.

growth.basis: Six audited/restated standalone annual revenues. No disclosed acquisition contribution; organic price/volume split ND; new IT support differs from SaaS.

market.basis: Secondary trade price and 31 March balance sheet, not current net debt. P/E uses current issued claims rather than historical weighted shares.

summary: Hold — unresolved. iCodex is a publishing-workflow technology and services business diversifying into domestic IT/project execution, not yet a demonstrated recurring SaaS compounder. Revenue grew at 39.18% over FY21–FY26, but FY26 PAT fell 20.80%, operating cash conversion was 0.23×, and capitalized development plus project deposits tie up substantial funding. The apparently modest 8.87× current-share P/E at the secondary ₹40.25 reference is not enough to overcome unresolved capital-application and funding bridges. BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS. This is a research-only execution/funding special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder or an instruction to trade. The decisive next evidence is a reconciled asset/proceeds ledger, accessible cash and facilities, collected project milestones and attributable software/project returns.
